title: Predict and control the biochemical organization of condensates

concept.text: The proposed innovation is the ability to predict how mixtures of proteins, RNA and other molecules organize into condensates, then deliberately change that organization to control a biochemical function. A useful prediction would explain which conditions produce an assembly, which molecules enter it, whether different assemblies remain separate, and what material properties they exhibit. Functional control would additionally require showing that a designed change produces the intended biochemical effect in cells.

The technical basis includes sequence-dependent interactions between intrinsically disordered protein regions—regions without a single fixed folded structure. Welles and colleagues showed that changes in selected disordered sequences and their chain-level properties can alter selective partitioning into distinct condensed phases. The broader innovation would extend such design principles to unfamiliar mixtures and cellular environments, beyond the selected engineered systems demonstrated in that study.

Three questions must remain separate: whether molecules assemble, whether the assembly has liquid material behavior, and whether it performs or changes a biochemical function. Proposed evaluation should therefore distinguish liquid phase separation from alternative explanations for visible cellular puncta, rather than treating appearance or colocalization alone as sufficient evidence.

significance.text: General predictive control would connect molecular chemistry to the emergence of organized biochemical compartments. Researchers could move from observing where molecules accumulate to designing selective recruitment and separation. The Welles study provides a technical rationale for this possibility through sequence engineering and selective partitioning, and discusses potential uses in synthetic organelles and pathway organization. These are anticipated applications, not demonstrations of general functional control.

As a conditional consequence, the capability could let researchers design where reactions occur, which molecules participate, and how local reaction environments change. Its revolutionary significance would come from transferring that control across unfamiliar systems, rather than optimizing one engineered condensate. Applications to gene expression, cellular engineering or disease treatment would require further evidence that the intended function changes reliably and that other cellular processes remain compatible with the intervention.

The analogy to designing an organelle has limits. Selective molecular recruitment does not by itself establish a complete functional compartment, and compartment formation does not guarantee a useful biochemical outcome. Predicting assembly, material behavior and function would each need validation; success in one does not establish the others.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is a predictive framework that transfers from molecular sequence and mixture conditions to selective organization and causal functional control in unfamiliar cellular settings. The supplied 2024 study documents a narrower historical challenge: predicting which disordered protein regions mix or separate from their sequences. It also explains why biochemical reconstitution may not reproduce cellular selectivity: components that form distinct phases outside cells can co-partition in the more complex cytosol.

Synthesis of the engineering challenge: a broadly useful framework would need to account for competing interactions among mixture components, their concentrations and the surrounding cellular context. The intended scope also includes modifications and cellular processes that change those interactions, but the supplied evidence does not establish how comprehensively existing methods handle these factors. Predicting formation, composition, material properties and function is a larger task than predicting selective mixing alone.

A further proposed requirement is a causal link between design and function. Changing a sequence or concentration may affect both assembly and other molecular activities. Convincing control would therefore require measurements and alternative-explanation controls that establish how the organizational change contributes to the functional outcome. The supplied study does not establish a general solution to that problem.

current_state.text: In the study published on 5 February 2024, Welles and colleagues combined experiments and molecular simulations to investigate why selected disordered protein regions form distinct condensed phases. Their principal systems were the FUS low-complexity region, FUS LC, and the LAF-1 arginine/glycine-rich region, LAF-1 RGG. Mutagenesis and changes to sequence-controlled chain properties altered selective partitioning, providing design principles for these systems.

The reported work included biochemical reconstitutions, engineered yeast systems, transfected HEK293T cells and a two-polymer simulation model. This scope matters: the findings extend beyond an isolated solution experiment, but they do not demonstrate a general predictive grammar for complex endogenous condensates. The supplied review identifies experiments, simulation and cellular portability results across the article, so the evidentiary basis is broader than the candidate’s original reference to the introduction and Figure 1 alone.

The supplied evidence establishes a dated technical advance, not a comprehensive account of the field through 1 November 2026. The accompanying search record is empty, leaving the later breadth and reliability of available prediction methods unverified. This limits any claim that all four outputs—phase behavior, composition, material properties and function—remain generally unpredictable; it does not establish that subsequent capabilities are absent or that the reported 2024 results are false.

The supplied review assessed the retained full article text, methods and legends, with no reported truncation or extraction issues. Figure images and linked supplementary material were not independently inspected. The account here therefore rests on the textual results described in that review; the supplied material provides no quantitative validation benchmark for the broader proposed capability.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: make blind predictions for diverse, previously untested mixtures across controlled conditions. Predictions should cover formation or absence of distinct assemblies, their major molecular components, selective mixing or separation, and relevant material properties. The mixture diversity, conditions, accuracy requirements and failure criteria should be specified before results are revealed. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established standards or thresholds supplied by the study.
completion_criteria.label: Blind predictions accurately characterize organization of diverse untested mixtures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional demonstration: use designed sequence or concentration changes to alter both organization and a prespecified biochemical function in cells. Measure assembly, liquid material behavior where claimed, composition and function separately. Include controls for alternative causes of puncta and for functional effects that could arise directly from the intervention without the proposed organizational mechanism.
completion_criteria.label: Designed changes control condensate organization and biochemical function in cells

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent groups should reproduce representative predictions and interventions, with documented conditions and measurement procedures. Evaluation should report where predictions fail, how performance changes between reconstituted and cellular systems, and which mixtures and cellular contexts have been tested. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproduction and reported prediction limits across tested systems

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” has the closest overlap. Both concern sequence-dependent interactions and environmental context, including disordered proteins. BCH-09 specifically requires prediction and functional control of emergent organization among multiple components; it cannot be reduced to assigning function to individual sequences.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-10, “Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks,” intersects where molecular modifications change interactions, recruitment or compartment composition. Its organizing question concerns modification-dependent networks, while BCH-09 concerns the formation, composition, material behavior and function of condensates. The supplied evidence does not establish a general modification-aware condensate model.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-01, “General design of enzymes for new chemical reactions,” concerns catalytic capability; BCH-09 could help organize enzymes and substrates spatially but would not itself establish new catalytic chemistry. BCH-03, “A self-maintaining, evolvable cell assembled from defined components,” could draw on designed biochemical compartments, but condensate control alone would not establish cellular self-maintenance or evolution.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-05, “Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading,” and BCH-06, “A multiplexed biochemical flight recorder for living cells,” could supply complementary measurements of molecular state or cellular history relevant to condensate behavior. Their central advances are measurement capabilities; BCH-09 requires prediction and causal intervention in biochemical organization.

change_log.change: Separated assembly, liquid material behavior and biochemical function, and treated punctum interpretation as an evaluation requirement.
change_log.reason: These require distinct evidence; the supplied paper does not directly substantiate the candidate’s broad punctum assertion.

change_log.reason: The source supplies an engineering rationale, not proof of general cellular functional control or clinical benefit.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include prespecified blind testing, causal controls, independent reproduction and explicit practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: The review supports these as proposals for evaluating generalization, while providing no consensus thresholds or claim of universal validation.

unresolved_issues: The supplied search record does not establish advances after the 2024 study or the field’s state through 1 November 2026.
How reliably existing methods jointly predict phase behavior, composition, material properties and function across unfamiliar cellular contexts remains unverified by the supplied evidence.

The broad roles of modifications and cellular processes, and the general assertion about alternative causes of cellular puncta, lack direct substantiation in the supplied evidence; they are retained as scope considerations and proposed evaluation requirements.
Mixture diversity, prediction accuracy thresholds, functional endpoints and acceptable practical limits remain to be specified for a convincing demonstration.
Figure images and linked supplementary material were not independently inspected in the supplied review; conclusions here rely on its assessment of the full article text, methods and legends.

brief.title: Predicting and controlling compartments inside cells
possible: Researchers could choose where reactions happen inside a cell and which molecules take part. They could predict how molecules gather into compartments without membranes, called condensates, then change their composition or physical state to produce a chosen effect.
why: This would let scientists building cellular systems organize reaction pathways and selectively bring molecules together or keep them apart. Control that works across unfamiliar mixtures would connect molecular design to the behavior of whole compartments.

sources.who: Rachel M Welles, Kandarp A Sojitra and colleagues
sources.showed: They changed protein regions without a fixed folded shape to alter which condensates the proteins joined.
sources.quote: We identified a pair of IDRs capable of forming spatially distinct condensates when expressed in cells.
sources.cited_for: Protein sequence can control whether selected proteins gather together or separately.
sources.not_established: The results do not establish predictions or functional control across unfamiliar cellular mixtures.

sources.who: Jonas Wessén, Nancy De La Cruz and colleagues
sources.showed: A model of repeated contacts between flexible protein chains predicted selective entry into condensates built from the protein MED1. Cellular experiments tested its predictions.
sources.quote: Here we show that a polymer physics-based model that only accounts for multivalent interactions among polymers in a statistical manner can largely explain published data on selective partitioning and make predictions that are subsequently experimentally validated.
sources.cited_for: Models can predict which proteins enter a particular condensate.
sources.not_established: Some predictions failed, and the model does not jointly predict formation, physical behavior and function across unfamiliar systems.

sources.showed: A model learned from experimental data predicted proteins likely to enter condensates and grouped them into predicted compartment types. Imaging supported many predictions.
sources.quote: Many of the top-ranked targets were later confirmed to localise into condensates by orthogonal immunohistochemical staining imaging.
sources.cited_for: Predicting condensate composition can extend beyond a single protein mixture.
sources.not_established: Some compartment regions were poorly distinguished, and composition predictions do not establish functional control.

sources.who: Min Lee, Hyungseok C Moon and colleagues
sources.showed: Light-controlled condensates trapped messenger RNA, the instructions for making proteins. More solid-like condensates suppressed protein production more strongly.
sources.quote: Using light-activated condensation, we show that sequestering target mRNAs into condensates causes translation inhibition.
sources.cited_for: Changing condensate organization and physical state can change a cellular function.
sources.not_established: This engineered system does not establish predictive functional control across diverse cellular contexts.

sources.showed: Designed proteins formed condensates in bacteria. Recruiting reaction pathways into them increased production of selected compounds.
sources.quote:
Through the targeted recruitment of biomolecules, our investigation demonstrates that
cellular condensates effectively sequester biosynthetic pathways.
sources.cited_for: Engineered condensates can organize cellular production pathways and change their output.
sources.not_established: Success in selected bacterial systems does not establish predictions and control that transfer to unfamiliar mixtures.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated parts of the capability. Welles and colleagues changed selective protein grouping through sequence design. Wessén and colleagues predicted entry into a particular condensate, while Saar and colleagues predicted components across several compartment types.

Functional control also exists in engineered systems. Lee and colleagues used light-controlled condensates to suppress protein production. Yu and colleagues built bacterial condensates that increased production of selected compounds.
missing: A framework must predict formation, composition and physical behavior together across diverse unfamiliar mixtures.
Designed changes must reliably control cellular function through compartment organization, with other effects ruled out.
Independent groups must reproduce representative predictions and interventions across clearly defined conditions.

milestones.label: Accurate blind predictions across diverse untested mixtures
milestones.explanation: Predictions would have to anticipate formation, contents, mixing and physical behavior under varied conditions, against criteria set before testing. This would establish predictive reach beyond familiar examples.

milestones.label: Designed cellular compartments produce the intended functional change
milestones.explanation: Designed changes would have to alter cellular organization and a chosen function, measuring each separately and ruling out other causes. This would establish that organization causes the intended effect.

milestones.label: Independent reproduction establishes where predictions work and fail
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to reproduce predictions and interventions and report failures across laboratory mixtures and cells. This would establish reliability and practical boundaries.

uncertain: How far can predictions transfer between simplified mixtures and the competing interactions inside cells?
Which mixture diversity, accuracy thresholds and functional outcomes would constitute a convincing demonstration?
How should tests distinguish assembly, liquid behavior and function when visible cellular spots alone cannot establish all of them?

page.title: Predictive design of biomolecular condensates
page.definition: A biomolecular condensate is a compartment whose molecular composition differs from its surroundings without an enclosing lipid membrane. From molecular sequences and cellular conditions, a model predicts whether a condensate forms, how strongly each component concentrates inside it, and how the material behaves, including how readily it flows. Given a desired biochemical effect in a cell, the model selects a change to the molecules or conditions that produces that effect.

goal.need: Microbial producers can test different ways of grouping pathway enzymes to see which gives more product. In a laboratory strain of Bacillus subtilis, bringing five enzymes together raised the concentration of 2′-fucosyllactose, a candidate infant-formula ingredient, from 328.0 to 681.6 mg/L. Predictive design would help producers choose an arrangement for higher yield or fewer by-products before building the strain. Its value depends on predicting both how much enzyme enters the compartment and how active it is there.

figures.caption: 2′-Fucosyllactose production in engineered Bacillus subtilis, reported 12 September 2024.
figures.note: Means from three biologically independent replicates per strain. YW15 is YW10 with condensates recruiting the five tagged pathway enzymes. Cultures used 30 mL medium in 250-mL shake flasks at 37 °C and 220 rpm.

completion.title: A fixed model prospectively predicts condensate organization and directs a biochemical effect in cells.
completion.criterion: Within a declared molecular and cellular domain, a model fixed before testing predicts phase formation, component partitioning and a material response for mixtures and cellular conditions excluded from fitting. Experiments match those predictions within stated measurement uncertainty, and an intervention selected by the model produces its predicted biochemical effect in cells. Condensation-specific perturbation and rescue controls establish that the organizational change causes the functional effect.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional synthesis of the published design goal and experimental recommendations.
completion.basis: Searches of NSF programme criteria, the 2019 guidelines, the 2025 community recommendations and the 2026 KITP roadmap, plus condensate benchmark, standards and prize searches, found no joint completion test or numerical accuracy cutoff. This criterion combines the roadmap’s specified composition, dynamics and material properties with controlled cellular function, within a declared domain.

milestones.title: A reconstituted mixture crosses a measured boundary from one phase to two coexisting phases.
milestones.criterion: For a reconstituted mixture, map conditions on both sides of the phase boundary. Identify conditions giving one homogeneous phase and conditions giving coexisting dilute and dense phases. Report the component concentrations and environmental conditions defining that boundary.
milestones.set_by: Alberti, Gladfelter and Mittag, 2019 experimental guidelines, phase-diagram discussion and Figure 1 caption.
milestones.threshold_quote: The coexistence line (black) separates the one-phase and two-phase regime and is a function of environmental conditions such as temperature, pH etc.

milestones.title: A protein mixture supports at least two mutually immiscible dense phases.
milestones.criterion: Show that at least two compositionally distinct dense phases coexist in the same mixture under the same conditions and remain distinct from one another. Identify the components enriched in each dense phase.
milestones.set_by: Alberti et al., 2025 community comment, definition of multiphase condensate architecture.

milestones.title: A condensate model matches measurements beyond the systems used to fit it.
milestones.criterion: Specify the class of condensates and the observable the model predicts. Compare predictions with measurements in systems from that class that were excluded from parameter fitting, and report the agreement. The community recommendation sets no numerical accuracy cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Alberti et al., 2025 community recommendations, model-selection section; a qualitative validation criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: features across diverse systems and matching experimental observations

milestones.title: Changing condensate properties changes cellular function while preserving other molecular activities.
milestones.criterion: Perturb a condensate property in cells and measure both the change in that property and the resulting change in cellular function. Show that the perturbed molecule retains the biochemical activities relevant to the assay outside the condensate. Test whether a change in soluble complexes could account for the phenotype.
milestones.set_by: Alberti et al., 2025 community recommendations, physical-property manipulation and cellular perturbation sections.
milestones.threshold_quote: if changes to the biophysical state alters functional output

milestones.title: A mechanical measurement quantifies the viscoelastic response of a condensate.
milestones.criterion: Measure the condensate’s response to deformation or infer it from the motion of embedded probes. Report a rheological quantity such as viscosity or an elastic modulus, the timescale of the measurement and, for embedded probes, the probe size relative to the condensate’s internal structure.
milestones.set_by: Alberti et al., 2025 community recommendations on measuring condensate material properties.
milestones.threshold_quote: Optical tweezers can be used to probe the viscoelasticity of condensates

milestones.title: A sequence selected for a target condensate shows the predicted pattern of enrichment.
milestones.criterion: Specify a target condensate and the intended distribution of a molecule, such as enrichment inside the condensate or at its interface. Use a model to select a sequence for that distribution before measuring it. Compare the measured distribution with the prediction and with a control sequence under the same conditions.
milestones.set_by: Prospective sequence-selection and localization assays used by Wessén et al. and in the experimental validation of interface-targeted peptides.
milestones.threshold_quote: identify novel sequences with high or low predicted PC values and test these predictions in the Lac array cell system.

not_found: No joint completion threshold or numerical accuracy requirement was found for predicting condensate organization and directing cellular biochemical function.
Searches of roadmaps, society statements and funding programmes found no body that judged predictive functional condensate design infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.

results.finding: The coarse-grained model correctly predicted condensate formation or absence for all five coiled-coil protein combinations in a blind test.
results.detail: Agreement was qualitative. In a separate comparison, the model predicted condensation for a 12-coil construct at 298 K that was not observed experimentally at lower temperatures.
results.quote:
The experimental observations—that protein combinations from b and
c form condensates, whereas combinations from a, d, and e do not —
were predicted by our simulation framework in a blind challenge.

results.finding: The 5-segment APPAP client enriched in APPAPAPPAP condensates. The recruitment sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The APPAP-alone condition tests whether the client self-condenses. A same-condition control for client recruitment would require a comparison sequence in the target condensate.
results.quote:
The
LLPS incompetent APPAP enriched to APPAPAPPAP condensates, act-
ing as a client (Supplementary Fig. 9).

results.finding: SRSF1 and Pol II IDR samples showed concentration-dependent phase separation in 3 independent in vitro experiments.
results.detail: Extended Data Fig. 2 lists concentrations at which individual IDRs form condensates. Those measurements give points on the phase-separated side only.

results.finding: Charged residues promoted immiscibility in a screen of 378 IDR pairs.
results.detail: The excerpt describes the two-color assays and their classification data. It gives no pair-specific dense-phase compositions.
results.quote: while charged amino acids drive immiscibility.

results.finding: Charge-rich fusions reduced Pol II condensate colocalization for 3 IDRs compared with their original sequences.
results.detail: Colocalization was quantified by Pearson r across fields of view. The excerpt supplies sample counts and the direction of change, with effect sizes left to the figure.

results.finding: Charge-fused IDRs showed lower Pol II miscibility and reduced IDR–SOX2 reporter activity, with 6 wells per construct.
results.detail: The charge perturbation could also affect molecular interactions outside condensates. The excerpt reports no controls that resolve that possibility.
results.quote: TFs with high overall charge content display reduced Pol II miscibility and impaired transcriptional output, and modulating charged residue content in TFs correspondingly tunes transcription.

results.finding: Six purified IDRs had dilute-phase saturation concentrations measured after phase separation at 150 mM NaCl.
results.detail: The supplied text points to supplementary tables for the individual concentrations and full experimental conditions.
results.quote: After desalting, phase separation was induced by adding NaCl to a final concentration of 150 mM, followed by centrifugation to separate the dense and dilute phase.

results.finding: Homotypic IDR condensates had a log saturation concentration RMSD of 1.12 across a wild-type benchmark that included six newly measured IDRs.
results.detail: The RMSD applies to the broader wild-type benchmark. The neural network was trained on CALVADOS 2 simulations. Some hnRNPA1 and LAF1 variant data in a separate benchmark had informed CALVADOS 2 parameterization.
results.quote:
We predicted saturation concentrations of the WT IDRs well, albeit with larger errors than for predictions of the simulation data (
RMSD
=
1.12
).

results.finding: One reconstituted RAD23A system showed an apparent phase-separation onset above 100 mM NaCl.
results.detail: Each reported turbidity value averaged ten consecutive readings from a single sample. The authors report independent replication of the observed trends without specifying a RAD23A replicate count.
results.quote: In agreement with the model’s predicted trend, turbidity measurements showed that RAD23A remained in a mixed state at low ionic strength (0–50 mM NaCl) but initiated phase separation above 100 mM

results.finding: LLPSense predicted single-protein phase separation with a mean AUROC of 0.77 across five cluster-held-out folds.
results.detail: The same cross-validation folds also informed hyperparameter selection. RAD23A provided a separate experimental comparison outside the training set.
results.quote: Under this cluster-based 5-fold CV, LLPSense demonstrated robust predictive performance, achieving an average AUROC of 0.77 and an AUPRC of 0.74

results.finding: In one DDX4N–peptide system, a possible second dense phase wetted the condensate.
results.detail: The mixture contained 10 µM DDX4N and 1 µM peptide in 20 mM Tris and 25 mM NaCl at pH 7.5. The supplied text gives no droplet count for the wetting observation.
results.quote: For DDX4N, and to some extent also for the other systems, interfacial localization is not perfectly uniform and results in multilayer adsorption or formation of a second phase wetting the condensates.

results.finding: Bulk dye lifetimes were unchanged after peptide addition in hnRNPA1-LCD and LAF-1-RGG condensates, with at least 25 condensates analyzed per image.
results.detail: The fluorescence lifetime characterizes the dye's response to its local environment. The study did not convert that lifetime to viscosity.
results.quote:
As shown in Fig.
4
D, the lifetime of both molecules in the interior of the condensates does not change upon peptide addition, suggesting a negligible effect of the peptide on the bulk.

results.finding: Predicted peptide interface enrichment agreed qualitatively with microscopy for all 3 tested protein-domain condensate targets.
results.detail: The final surrogate for each target was trained on the entire available simulation dataset. The microscopy measurements followed design and were separate from the simulation data used to fit the surrogate.
results.quote: Interfacial accumulation of the designed peptides was experimentally confirmed in vitro for all three cases, validating the design approach.

results.finding: Designed peptides enriched at the interfaces of all 3 tested condensate targets while matched controls distributed through the dense phase.
results.detail: The targets were hnRNPA1-LCD, LAF-1-RGG, and DDX4N. The DDX4N interface enrichment was uneven. The supplied text does not give the droplet count behind the 91% coverage result.

results.finding: Of four charge-balanced ProTα mixtures mapped, ProTα–R50 still formed coexisting phases above 1 M KCl.
results.detail: The microscopy confirms coexistence at 90 mM KCl. The prose describes phase separation of the lysine-rich mixtures as difficult above 200 mM KCl without specifying a measured homogeneous condition.
results.quote: Phase separation is difficult to achieve above 200 mM KCl for the lysine-rich polypeptides, but the arginine-rich polypeptides readily phase-separate with ProTα at higher salt—for R50 even above 1 M KCl.

results.finding: In four ProTα coacervate formulations, bead tracking (n ≥ 20 beads for the reported error bands) found bulk viscosity up to ~10,000 times that of water.
results.quote: The viscosity in the droplets is remarkably different for complex coacervates with different polycationic proteins and ranges from ~300 to ~10,000 times the viscosity of water ( Fig. 2 I ).

results.finding: For 3 disordered-protein condensates outside the fit, published viscosity and diffusion data followed the entangled Rouse prediction.
results.detail: The external comparisons are indicative because the fitted tube diameter may differ across systems. Reconfiguration times for the three external protein condensates were predictions without corresponding measurements in the comparison.
results.quote: Remarkably, all of these data are in line with the behavior of the coacervates studied here ( Fig. 4 D )

results.finding: Homozygous NDF K161A human iPS cells had ~25% fewer Spt16 puncta than wild type (56 wild-type and 43 mutant technical replicates).
results.detail: K161A disrupts one Spt16 interaction site while leaving binding through the PWWP domain intact. This leaves open whether soluble NDF–FACT complexes behave differently in mutant cells.
results.quote: Immunofluorescence revealed ~25% reduction in Spt16 puncta number and dimmer remaining foci in NDF_K161A cells

results.finding: In 155,584 G3BP1–HeLa lysate microdroplets, a measured binodal separated homogeneous and two-phase conditions, with stress granules forming over ~3–40 µM G3BP1.
results.detail: The concentration ranges describe the region where condensates formed. The phase diagrams plot the binodal itself. Lysate concentration is expressed as total protein and represents dilution of the retained lysate, including RNA and other soluble components.
results.quote: In both cases, sharp binodal boundaries separated homogeneous and phase-separated regions, providing a quantitative map of the conditions under which condensates assemble.

results.finding: A purified FIB1–NPM1 mixture formed 2 mutually immiscible dense phases in vitro (replicate count unreported).
results.detail: At lower concentrations of either protein, the mixture formed a single dense phase enriched in the other protein.
results.quote: High concentrations of both proteins (FIB1: 2.5 μM, NPM1: 10 μM) give rise to FIB1-rich droplets (green) which are immiscible with and partially enveloped by NPM1-rich droplets (red).

definition = "A biomolecular condensate is a compartment whose molecular composition differs from its surroundings without an enclosing lipid membrane. From molecular sequences and cellular conditions, a model predicts whether a condensate forms, how strongly each component concentrates inside it, and how the material behaves, including how readily it flows. Given a desired biochemical effect in a cell, the model selects a change to the molecules or conditions that produces that effect.". Reason: The definition leaves partitioning and material properties abstract and gives little indication of how a desired cellular effect guides the choice of molecules.

goal.need = "Microbial producers can test different ways of grouping pathway enzymes to see which gives more product. In a laboratory strain of Bacillus subtilis, bringing five enzymes together raised the concentration of 2\u2032-fucosyllactose, a candidate infant-formula ingredient, from 328.0 to 681.6 mg/L. Predictive design would help producers choose an arrangement for higher yield or fewer by-products before building the strain. Its value depends on predicting both how much enzyme enters the compartment and how active it is there.". Reason: The protein count and replicate count give no measure of the consequence for production, whereas the matched strains quantify it and enzyme activity explains why recruitment alone cannot predict it.

edit m1: criterion = "For a reconstituted mixture, map conditions on both sides of the phase boundary. Identify conditions giving one homogeneous phase and conditions giving coexisting dilute and dense phases. Report the component concentrations and environmental conditions defining that boundary.". Reason: The original criterion mixes the phase-boundary test with a salt concentration, temperature and replicate count specific to one experiment.

edit m2: criterion = "Show that at least two compositionally distinct dense phases coexist in the same mixture under the same conditions and remain distinct from one another. Identify the components enriched in each dense phase.". Reason: The original criterion mixes coexistence of two dense phases with a recruitment assay in which a dilute protein was tested for entry into one dense phase.

add milestone after m2: "A mechanical measurement quantifies the viscoelastic response of a condensate.". Reason: The completion test requires a material response, but none of the existing milestones requires a quantitative measurement of that response.

edit m3: criterion = "Specify the class of condensates and the observable the model predicts. Compare predictions with measurements in systems from that class that were excluded from parameter fitting, and report the agreement. The community recommendation sets no numerical accuracy cutoff.". Reason: The two published success rates describe different prediction tasks and obscure the common requirement to test the model beyond the systems used to fit it.

add milestone after m3: "A sequence selected for a target condensate shows the predicted pattern of enrichment.". Reason: Agreement on independent data leaves open whether a model can select a molecule for a specified location and have that choice confirmed experimentally.

edit m4: criterion = "Perturb a condensate property in cells and measure both the change in that property and the resulting change in cellular function. Show that the perturbed molecule retains the biochemical activities relevant to the assay outside the condensate. Test whether a change in soluble complexes could account for the phenotype.". Reason: The original criterion interleaves two cellular results with the controls needed to attribute a change in function to condensate properties.
remove not found 1. Reason: The full Welles et al. author manuscript, including the cellular and reconstitution experiments, is publicly available in PubMed Central as PMC11929961.

add not found: "Searches of roadmaps, society statements and funding programmes found no body that judged predictive functional condensate design infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.".
